card.name: Time units ending dose schedules
card.fires_on: The time or frequency word that completes a dosing schedule or infusion duration, such as minutes after 'over 30', weeks after 'every 2', or times and once in 'four times a day'.

modes.label: Infusion duration
modes.description: The unit 'minutes' ending an infusion length after a number.
modes.example: Administer doses greater than 500 mg by intravenous infusion over 40 to 60<< minutes>>.

modes.label: Dosing frequency
modes.description: The last word of a frequency phrase such as every 2 weeks, four times a day, or once daily.
modes.example: the dosage may be adjusted 150 mg subcutaneously every 2<< weeks>>.

modes.label: Schedule nouns
modes.description: A schedule noun like Day, infusion or intervals completing a named timing term.
modes.example: This day is known as the “Patch Change<< Day>>.”

card.writes: Little clear signal; the promoted tokens suggest ideas of staying unchanged or undergoing change, while process-ending words are suppressed.
card.plain: It lights up on the word that finishes how long or how often a dose is given, like minutes or weeks.
